newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds plunge on U.S. rate rise fears.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds plunge on U.S. rate rise fears.

text.p: Argentine bonds plunged on Tuesday after a drop in U.S. Treasuries reversed the strong surge of recent days.

"The market fell on a mix of an end to the short-covering of recent days and the rise in the U.S. long bond," said the head trader at an Argentine bank. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.80 to 117.75, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 1-1/8 to 82-1/2.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Provisional 2 due 2007 fell $0.20 to 101.90.

Traders voiced some surprise that the market fell so heavily considering the fairly strong mood at the opening. Mainly foreign investors were reported on the sell side this session, said the head trader.

The market turnaround was sparked by a Reuters report saying that eight of 12 district banks in the U.S. Federal Reserve System have requested a rise in the 5.0 percent discount rate amid mounting evidence the pace of U.S. expansion is likely to remain brisk in the second half of 1996.
That report took away one of the key building blocks that helped fuel the Latin American markets' surge in recent days -- that U.S. rates are likely to remain on hold this month.
With the report, Argentine bonds' continued rise is likely to be much more dependent on the fortunes of U.S. Treasuries.
"If the U.S. long bond does not over-exaggerate, the market should be able rise again," said the trader.

After this session's shakeout, U.S. markets allowing, Wednesday's debate in Argentina's Congress on the government's tax hiking measures could restore some confidence said traders. The market has discounted that Congress attains a quorum on the measures.
Separately this session, Argentina sold $250 million treasury bills (Letes) at a cut-off yield of 6.10 percent. The bid-to-cover ratio was 3.05 times.
In the money markets, one day call money rates fell to 6.63 percent from 6.65 percent.
